Apple paid Creative US$100 million to settle their 2006 suit.
In January 2007, the iPod market share reached 72.7%.
Since October 2004, the iPod line has dominated digital music player sales in the United States, with over 90% of the market for hard drive-based players.
On January 8, 2004, Hewlett-Packard unveiled their own edition of the iPod.
Unfavorable terms and conditions imposed by Apple led HP to leave the iPod market.
Apple revealed it sold its one-hundred millionth iPod in April 2007.
Apple revealed it had achieved its highest quarterly earnings to date on January 22, 2008.
42% of Apple's revenue for the First fiscal quarter of 2008 came from iPod sales, more than doubling the percentage of notebook sales at 21%.
